items.stem: Felix finds angle ABC for A(−4, 0, 4), B(−3, 1, −3), C(0, −1, 4) using the vectors AB and BC and obtains 149°. Explain the error and find the correct angle.
items.markingKey: The angle at B is between BA and BC (both from B) (R1); using AB reverses one vector and gives the supplement (R1); correct angle 180° − 149° = 31.4° (A1).

items.stem: Amara writes: "The magnitude of (3, −4) is −1 because 3 + (−4) = −1." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Magnitude is √(3² + (−4)²) = 5; it is never negative.
items.markingKey: Magnitude is √(3² + (−4)²) = 5; it is never negative. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain how you would use vectors to decide whether A(1, 0, −2), B(3, 0, −2), C(3, 2, 1), D(1, 2, 1) is a rectangle, and carry out the test.
items.markingKey: AB = DC = (2, 0, 0) so ABCD is a parallelogram (M1 R1); AB·AD = 0 = 0 so adjacent sides are perpendicular (M1); hence a rectangle (R1).

items.stem: Explain why the scalar product is commutative.
items.answer: v·w = Σvᵢwᵢ = Σwᵢvᵢ = w·v, since multiplication of numbers is commutative.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: v·w = Σvᵢwᵢ = Σwᵢvᵢ = w·v, since multiplication of numbers is commutative. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Determine whether the vectors (−1, −4, −4) and (3, 12, 12) are parallel, explaining your reasoning.
items.markingKey: Parallel iff one is a scalar multiple of the other (R1); compare component ratios (M1); conclusion: parallel: second = −3 × first (A1).

items.stem: Explain how you would use vectors to decide whether A(1, −2, −2), B(3, −2, −2), C(3, 0, 1), D(1, 0, 1) is a rectangle, and carry out the test.
items.markingKey: AB = DC = (2, 0, 0) so ABCD is a parallelogram (M1 R1); AB·AD = 0 = 0 so adjacent sides are perpendicular (M1); hence a rectangle (R1).

items.stem: Elena writes: "If a·b = a·c then b = c." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: It only means a·(b − c) = 0, i.e. b − c is perpendicular to a (or zero); b and c can differ.

Two ships A and B have position vectors rA = (−4, 1) + t(−2, −4) and rB = (−3, −1) + t(0, −1) (km) at time t hours. Find the time at which they are closest together and the minimum distance between them.
items.markingKey: AB = rB − rA = (2t + 1, 3t − 2) (M1 A1); |AB|² = 13t² − 8t + 5 (A1); minimise: d/dt = 0 (M1) t = 0.308 (A1); distance 1.94 km (A1).

items.stem:
The points A(−2, −5, 2), B(5, 2, 1) and C(1, −5, 1) are three vertices of the parallelogram ABCD.
(a) Find the vectors AB and BC.
(b) Find the coordinates of D.
(c) Find the coordinates of the point where the diagonals intersect.
(d) Find the exact lengths of the diagonals AC and BD and hence determine whether ABCD is a rectangle.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1. (b) AD = BC so OD = a + BC (M1) = (−6, −12, 2) (A1). (c) midpoint of AC (M1) (−1/2, −5, 3/2) (A1). (d) |AC| = √10, |BD| = √318 (A1 A1); a parallelogram is a rectangle iff its diagonals are equal (R1): not a rectangle (A1).

items.stem:
A rectangular room OABCDEFG has O at the origin, OA along the x-axis with OA = 8 m, OC along the y-axis with OC = 3 m and OD vertical with OD = 8 m; G is the vertex opposite O. M is the midpoint of the edge CB.
(a) Write down the position vectors of G and M.
(b) Find the length of the diagonal OG.
(c) Find the angle between OG and the base OABC.
(d) Find the angle GOM.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1. (b) √(8² + 3² + 8²) (M1) = 11.7 (A1). (c) angle with projection (√(73) on base) (M1); tan θ = 8/√73 (A1); 43.1° (A1). (d) OG·OM = 41 (A1); cos θ = OG·OM/(|OG||OM|) (M1); 45.5° (A1).

items.stem: Explain how the sign of v·w tells you whether the angle between v and w is acute or obtuse.
items.answer: v·w has the sign of cos θ: positive for acute θ, zero for a right angle, negative for obtuse θ.

items.stem: Explain why AB = b − a.
items.answer: Travel from A back to O and then from O to B: AB = AO + OB = −a + b.

items.stem: Maya writes: "A quadrilateral with equal diagonals is a rectangle." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Equal diagonals alone are not enough (an isosceles trapezium also has them); a parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle.
items.markingKey: Equal diagonals alone are not enough (an isosceles trapezium also has them); a parallelogram with equal diagonals is a rectangle. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: "|a + b| = |a| + |b| for all vectors a and b." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: This only holds if a and b point in the same direction; in general |a + b| ≤ |a| + |b| (triangle inequality).

items.stem:
In triangle OAB, OA = a and OB = b. M is the midpoint of OA and N is the point on OB with ON : NB = 2 : 3.
(a) Express AB, MN and AN in terms of a and b.
(b) The point P lies on AN such that MP is parallel to OB. Find AP : PN.
items.answer: (a) AB = b − a, MN = 2/5b − ½a, AN = 2/5b − a (b) AP : PN = 1 : 1
items.markingKey: (a) A1 A1 A1. (b) Let OP = a + λAN (M1); MP = OP − OM = (½ − λ)a + λ(2/5)b (A1); parallel to b requires ½ − λ = 0 (M1), λ = ½ (A1) so P is the midpoint of AN, AP : PN = 1 : 1 (A1).
